Any divergence means resumed events belong to a different causal identity, making the append-only log internally inconsistent\u2014a single log containing events from two causally distinct runs.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the system explicitly models resumption as a new causal segment (e.g., a 'resume' event with its own fingerprint), then a different fingerprint is acceptable as long as it is declared.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If model state is nondeterministic by design (e.g., stochastic sampling), exact fingerprint matching is impossible and the criterion would forbid all resumption, which is too strict.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the program is interpreted and minor implementation changes don't alter observable behavior, exact hash matching is overly brittle.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The identity of an event stream is not merely 'the same log file' but 'the same causal origin.' An event's identity is determined by the causal process that generated it: (program, inputs, model state). If any component changes (e.g., model weights updated, program patched, input modified), the resumed events are causally alien to the pre-interruption events. Inserting them into the same append-only log creates a Frankenstein stream: structurally append-only but causally incoherent. The fingerprint check is the gatekeeper.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
